concerns: The paper repeatedly claims to analyze accuracy-latency-energy trade-offs and to examine quantization and runtime optimizations, but no accuracy metrics, quantization ablations, or runtime-optimization results are reported anywhere in the tables, figures, or text.

The evaluated neural network architectures are not specified: the custom 2D and 3D CNN structures, layer configurations, and implementation details are omitted, preventing reproducibility of the reported measurements.

The abstract claims a reproducible evaluation framework, but the methodology reports only three repetitions with the most stable run selected, no uncertainty or variability statistics, and no code, model definitions, or data-processing details sufficient for independent replication.
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: The empirical profiling data for runtime and power on the selected devices is clear, but the absence of model classification accuracy metrics, omission of network architectural specifications, and unfulfilled claims regarding quantization and runtime optimization evaluations create substantial scientific uncertainty.

gesture recognition and face-mask detection—across three distinct embedded edge computing

For mask detection, we evaluate two model families: a lightwe ight 2D CNN on the RMFD 
dataset (inputs at 300 × 300 and 516 × 516), and a ResNet-50 on the MaskedFace-Net dataset (224 
× 224 and 960 × 544). This combination reflects both constrained and computationally demanding 
pipelines, and allows us to capture how model capacity interacts with device limitations. 
All devices were configured in performance-oriented modes to reduce throttling and stabilize 
results. On Jetson boards, experiments were run under JetPack environments (v6.0 for AGX Orin 
and v4.2.1 for Nano), while the Raspberry Pi used Raspbian with TensorFlow/PyTorch backends.

evidence.excerpt:
variance. Unless otherwise 
specified, batch size = 1 and single-stream inference were used. 
Measurements were taken under consistent conditions. Latency is reported as the median 
inference time over repeated runs after discarding warm-up iterations. Memory usage reflects 
peak resident set size (RSS) during inference. CPU and GPU power draw were recorded through 
on-device telemetry (tegrastats for Jetson boards and vcgencmd for Raspberry Pi) at 1 Hz 
sampling, then averaged. To account for runtime variability, each experiment was repeated three 
times, and the most stable run was reported. 
This setup provides a transparent basis for comparing devices with widely different compute 
capabilities, memory budgets, and power envelopes, and lays the foundation for the 
benchmarking results reported in Section 3.2.

memory requirements approximately 2.0–2.8 GB on Orin, 1.5–2.15 GB on Nano, and 0.8–0.83 GB 
on Raspberry Pi 3. These findings highlight that model capacity (such as ResNet-50) is typically 
the primary factor that limits performance on lower-end hardware.

blocking_reasons: The paper repeatedly claims to analyze accuracy-latency-energy trade-offs and to examine quantization and runtime optimizations, but no accuracy metrics, quantization ablations, or runtime-optimization results are reported anywhere in the tables, figures, or text.

The evaluated neural network architectures are not specified: the custom 2D and 3D CNN structures, layer configurations, and implementation details are omitted, preventing reproducibility of the reported measurements.

The abstract claims a reproducible evaluation framework, but the methodology reports only three repetitions with the most stable run selected, no uncertainty or variability statistics, and no code, model definitions, or data-processing details sufficient for independent replication.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The study does not optimize against an evaluator; reported outcomes are direct hardware measurements rather than scores from a learned or automated judge.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Hardware profiling metrics: median inference latency, peak resident set size, and on-device CPU/GPU power telemetry.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: No model training, tuning, selection, or optimization loop is described; the study profiles pre-existing model configurations on fixed hardware.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: There is a notable mismatch between claims and evidence: the abstract and text assert examination of quantization, runtime optimizations, and speed-accuracy trade-offs, yet no model accuracy figures or quantization ablation experiments are provided in the tables or figures.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation consists solely of empirical inference measurements presented in Table 2. Crucially, task accuracy metrics (e.g., Top-1 accuracy, mAP, precision/recall) are completely absent despite repeated claims in the text about analyzing accuracy-latency-energy trade-offs.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The paper does not involve an automated tuning loop or adaptive evaluator, relying purely on hardware profiling instrumentation.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: System profiling metrics including inference latency (ms), peak resident memory (GB), and on-device telemetry power draw (mW).
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Not applicable as no model training, tuning, or optimization algorithm was developed or iteratively guided in the study.

primary.limitations: The work does not adequately address its failure to report model accuracy, omit detailed architectural details of the tested networks, or explain the discrepancy between claimed quantization studies and reported results.
primary.method_assessment: While the experimental hardware profiling setup is described (single-stream batch size 1 inference, locked GPU clocks, tegrastats/vcgencmd sampling), essential architectural specifications of the evaluated neural network models (e.g., custom 2D/3D CNN layer structures and implementation details) are omitted. Claims regarding the evaluation of quantization and runtime optimizations mentioned in the abstract are not described or evidenced in the methodology.
primary.quality_rationale: The empirical profiling data for runtime and power on the selected devices is clear, but the absence of model classification accuracy metrics, omission of network architectural specifications, and unfulfilled claims regarding quantization and runtime optimization evaluations create substantial scientific uncertainty.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper presents an empirical benchmarking study profiling latency, peak resident memory, and CPU/GPU power draw across three embedded hardware platforms (NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, Jetson Nano, and Raspberry Pi 3) executing 2D and 3D CNN architectures on gesture recognition and face mask datasets.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The empirical profiling data for runtime and power on the selected devices is clear, but the absence of model classification accuracy metrics, omission of network architectural specifications, and unfulfilled claims regarding quantization and runtime optimization evaluations create substantial scientific uncertainty.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The work does not adequately address its failure to report model accuracy, omit detailed architectural details of the tested networks, or explain the discrepancy between claimed quantization studies and reported results.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
